questions.question: What did historical ancient ideas suggest about the Earth's shape and the movement of astronomical bodies?
options: Earth was flat, with all the stars and the Sun moving around it
Earth was a sphere that rotated while stars remained stationary
Earth was a flat disk that orbited a stationary Sun
Earth was a sphere located at the edge of a flat universe

questions.question: Until which century did most people believe that Earth was located at the centre of the universe?
options: The 12th century
The 14th century
The 16th century
The 18th century

questions.question: Which tool provides crucial observational evidence that helps us to understand the universe?
options: The microscope
The telescope
The barometer
The seismometer

questions.question: What is the approximate angle of tilt of the axis on which the Earth spins?
options: 12.5 degrees
23.5 degrees
45.0 degrees
90.0 degrees

questions.question: In which direction does gravity pull objects when they are near massive bodies like planets, moons, or stars?
options: Away from the body into deep space
Towards the centre of the massive object
In a clockwise direction around the surface
Towards the magnetic north pole of the object

questions.question: What is the relationship between the mass of an object and the strength of its gravity?
options: The greater the mass of an object, the stronger its gravity
The greater the mass of an object, the weaker its gravity
The mass of an object does not affect its gravitational strength
Gravity increases only when the mass of an object decreases

questions.question: How does the gravitational pull of a planet, moon, or star change with distance?
options: It remains completely constant regardless of distance
It gets stronger the further you travel into space
It extends far into space, but gets weaker with distance
It drops to absolute zero immediately outside the atmosphere

questions.question: How does Earth's gravity affect the motion of the Moon?
options: It pushes the Moon further away into space every year
It pulls the Moon towards the centre of Earth, changing its direction and making it orbit
It causes the Moon to spin much faster on its own axis
It heats up the surface of the Moon through constant gravitational friction

questions.question: What keeps the Earth orbiting around the Sun rather than flying off into deep space?
options: The Sun's magnetic field pushing Earth sideways
The pressure of light rays acting as a solar sail
The Sun's gravity pulling Earth towards the centre of the Sun, changing its direction
Earth's own atmosphere acting as a propeller through space

questions.question: How does the effectiveness of heating a surface from directly overhead compare to heating it at an angle?
options: Heating from directly overhead is less effective than heating at an angle
Heating from directly overhead is more effective than heating at an angle
There is no difference in heating effectiveness
Heating at an angle is always twice as effective as heating from directly overhead

questions.question: What happens to rays of light when they hit a surface face-on rather than at an angle?
options: They are more spread out over a larger area
They are less spread out than if they hit at an angle
They reflect completely and produce no heating effect
They bend at ninety degrees and travel along the surface

questions.question: How do the distances between objects in our solar system compare to the actual physical sizes of the objects themselves?
options: The distances are extremely small compared to the sizes of the objects
The distances are roughly equal to the diameters of the planets
The distances are very, very large compared to the sizes of the objects
The objects are so large that they almost touch each other

questions.question: Why do countries located near the Equator not experience distinct summer and winter seasons?
options: They stay close to 'face-on' to the Sun all year
They are tilted away from the Sun during the entire year
They do not receive any direct sunlight because of cloud cover
The Earth's tilt does not affect the Equator's distance from the Sun

questions.question: What is a light-year, and why is it used by astronomers?
options: The time it takes for Earth to orbit the Sun, used to measure planetary ages
The distance light travels in one year, which is suitable for vast distances in space
The speed at which light travels through the solar system
The distance from the Earth to the nearest star

questions.question: What is a galaxy in the context of the universe?
options: A small cloud of dust orbiting a single star
A group of stars containing exactly eight planets
A group of stars, with billions of stars in each group
A single massive star that has exploded

questions.question: Which of the following describes the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun?
options: A highly elongated, stretched-out oval
An almost perfect circle
A perfect square with rounded corners
A spiral that gets closer to the Sun every year
